title.value: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021
title.justification: The title concisely highlights the main focus of the paper, which is to review and analyze standardized seroprevalence studies of SARS-CoV-2 infection across Africa within a specified time frame.
title.quote: SARS-­CoV-­2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-­analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021

extractions.description: This paper presents a systematic review and meta-analysis of seroprevalence studies conducted in Africa to estimate the seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2. It aims to improve understanding of COVID-19 exposure in Africa, assisting in public health decision-making and vaccination strategies.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper focuses on public health surveillance and understanding the spread of SARS-CoV-2 in Africa, it does not directly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Estimating COVID-­19 cumulative incidence in Africa remains problematic due to challenges in contact tracing, routine surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacities and strategies. We undertook a meta-­analysis of population-­based seroprevalence studies to estimate SARS-­CoV-­2 seroprevalence in Africa to inform evidence-­based decision making on public health and social measures (PHSM) and vaccine strategy.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on epidemiological analysis related to SARS-CoV-2 and public health in Africa and does not align directly with any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category.
primary_category.quote: Conclusion We report high seroprevalence in Africa suggesting greater population exposure to SARS-­CoV-­2 and potential protection against COVID-­19 severe disease than indicated by surveillance data.

secondary_categories.justification: As the primary focus is epidemiology and public health regarding SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa, there are no secondary themes relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: We estimate that overall seroprevalence is high in Africa (65.1% in Q3 2021) and has risen considerably over time, from 3.0% (1.0%–9.2%) in Q2 2020, marked by sharp increases after the emergence of the Beta and Delta variants.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's content on COVID-19 seroprevalence studies does not align with any defined sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Methods We searched for seroprevalence studies conducted in Africa published 1 January 2020–30 December 2021.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As with the primary sub-category, the paper's focus does not intersect with any secondary sub-categories relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Results We identified 56 full texts or early results, reporting 153 distinct seroprevalence studies in Africa.

applications.value: Public health decision-making and vaccine strategy support in Africa
applications.justification: The paper informs evidence-based decision-making on public health and vaccination strategies by analyzing the seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 across Africa.
applications.quote: We undertook a meta­analysis of population­based seroprevalence studies to estimate SARS­CoV­2 seroprevalence in Africa to inform evidence­based decision making on public health and social measures (PHSM) and vaccine strategy.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's alignment with public health research is clear, focusing on COVID-19 seroprevalence in Africa and informing policy and vaccination strategies, an aspect not covered by existing sustainable development categories.
new_primary_category.quote: Our results suggest that the ratio of seroprevalence to cumulative incidence of confirmed cases is large (100:1 (83:1­115:1)) in Africa overall, varying from 18:1 to 954:1 by country over the study period.

new_primary_sub_category.value: Epidemiology and Vaccine Strategy in Africa
new_primary_sub_category.justification: This sub-category aptly describes the paper's focus on epidemiological studies to support vaccine strategies and public health responses specifically within the African context, connecting directly to the paper's content and purpose.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We aimed to better understand SARS-­CoV-­2 epidemiology in Africa up to and before the emergence of the Omicron variant.
